headline: Adopted bonds for wastewater plant upgrades, DPW garage, and pool repairs; tabled landfill bonds; adopted ordinance allowing remote public comment for disabled residents.
summary: The board approved contracts for a copier lease, internet service, and software program, plus wastewater treatment plant construction ($11,692,041.56) and engineering ($1,361,000) contracts. It adopted bond resolutions for sewer, wastewater, pool, and DPW garage projects, tabled a $2,000,000 bond for Four Hills Landfill improvements, and adopted an ordinance allowing remote public comment for people with disabilities. It also confirmed board appointments and referred new resolutions and ordinances to committees.
decisions: Accepted a communication on energy contract savings and cost avoidance and placed it on file.
Accepted a communication on the disposition of 342 Main Street and placed it on file.
Approved a copier lease and maintenance contract with Toshiba Financial Services not to exceed $35,220.
Approved a 36-month internet service contract extension with Fidium Enterprise Services, LLC not to exceed $29,484.
Approved a 3-year Microsoft Software Assurance Program contract with SHI International Corp. not to exceed $68,310.08.
Approved a construction contract with Loureiro Building Construction, LLC for the Wastewater Treatment Facility Phase I Upgrade, not to exceed $11,692,041.56, contingent on additional bond funding.
Approved a construction administration services contract with Wright Pierce for the Wastewater Treatment Facility Phase I Upgrade, not to exceed $1,361,000.
Approved Change Order #1 with N.E. Mobile Audio for the Renaissance Park audio system, not to exceed $3,597.00.
Approved waiving the City's right of first refusal for the NHDOT right-of-way adjacent to Main Dunstable Road.
Confirmed the re-appointment of Charles Emmons to the Arts Commission with a term to expire July 30, 2029.
Confirmed the re-appointment of Carl Andrade to the Business and Industrial Development Authority with a term to expire September 13, 2028.
Confirmed the re-appointment of Frank Teas to the Electric Aggregation Committee with a term to expire August 31, 2028.
Confirmed new appointments of Jane Goodman, LaTonya Muccioli, and Tonia Knisley to the Homeless Services Gap Analysis Committee.
Adopted R-26-057, borrowing an additional $345,000 from the Clean Water State Revolving Fund for the Four Hills Landfill PFAS/leachate removal pilot project, by a 13-0 roll call vote.
Adopted R-26-059, authorizing borrowing not to exceed $3,000,000 for the Wastewater Treatment Plant Phase 1 Upgrades Project, by an 11-2 roll call vote.
Adopted R-26-060, authorizing bonds not to exceed $4,275,000 for sewer infrastructure improvement and casting replacement programs, by a 12-1 roll call vote.
Adopted R-26-061, authorizing bonds not to exceed $2,550,000 for various wastewater capital improvements, by an 11-2 roll call vote.
Tabled R-26-062, which would authorize bonds not to exceed $2,000,000 for improvements at the Four Hills Landfill, by a 10-3 roll call vote.
Adopted R-26-063, authorizing bonds not to exceed $2,678,828 for solid waste capital equipment, by a 12-1 roll call vote.
Adopted R-26-065, transferring $150,000 from the School computer equipment account to the Food Services Fund for FY2026 expenditures.
Adopted R-26-066, authorizing bonds not to exceed $5,000,000 for repair and renovation of two public inground swimming pools, by a 12-1 roll call vote.
Adopted R-26-072, authorizing bonds not to exceed $43,500,000 for a new Division of Public Works garage and fleet maintenance facility, by a 12-1 roll call vote.
Adopted R-26-073, changing the purpose of up to $3,183,200 of unexpended bond proceeds to the DPW garage and fleet maintenance project, by an 11-2 roll call vote.
Adopted R-26-074, creating three expendable trust funds and transferring $790,387 from prior year escrows for various infrastructure and maintenance projects.
Approved withdrawing R-26-064 from the Budget Review Committee for a second reading.
Approved amending R-26-064 by replacing it with a handout from Treasurer/Tax Collector Mulholland.
Referred R-26-064 as amended to the Budget Review Committee and set its public hearing for October 26th.
Approved amending O-26-002's title and adding Section 12 on electronic public comment for people with disabilities, by a 10-3 roll call vote.
Adopted O-26-002 as amended, allowing electronic public comment for people with disabilities, by a 10-3 roll call vote.
Referred R-26-075, on a federal aid bridge rehabilitation agreement accepting an additional $231,941.29, to the Finance Committee for first reading.
Referred R-26-076, on accepting $45,180 from the U.S. Department of Justice for a police grant, to the Human Affairs Committee for first reading.
Referred O-26-025, increasing the elderly and disabled tax exemption income limits, to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee and Board of Assessors for first reading.
Referred O-26-026, on approvals for gasoline, electricity, and natural gas contracts, to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee for first reading.

From: Liz Hannum, Economic Development Director 
MEMO Re: Disposition of 342 Main Street 
 
 
The City recently issued a Request for Proposals for the purchase and redevelopment of 342 Main Street, a 
tax-deeded property owned by the City. Prior to issuance of the RFP, the City completed all required notices 
and procedures associated with disposition of the property, including providing any parties with applicable 
repurchase rights the opportunity to exercise those rights. 
The City received one proposal in response to the RFP, submitted by Habitat for Humanity. Habitat 
proposes to purchase the property and construct an owner-occupied duplex, creating two new affordable 
homeownership opportunities at the site.  
Following review of the proposal, the City is recommending award of the project to Habitat for Humanity, 
subject to approval by the Board of Aldermen. The intent to award letter is attached. The proposed 
redevelopment will return a tax-deeded property to productive use, add new housing, support 
homeownership opportunities, and return the property to the tax rolls. 
City staff will bring a Purchase and Sale and Master Development Agreement in the coming months for your 
approval.
